plan.focus: The gap between Morton's 285 at-bats and Reyna's 164 is the whole argument — one man proved he can handle a season, the other proved he can handle a matchup.
plan.why: The claim has to stand on the season line before it stands on narrative. Morton's .291 over 285 at-bats is the only number in the group that carries the weight of a full-time answer. Reyna's .317 is real, but 164 at-bats is a half-season of selective exposure. The squeeze resolves itself if you trust the larger sample.
